title: The Ass and the Lapdog
text:
A farmer kept an ass and a little lapdog. The ass lived in the stable, had plenty of hay and oats, and worked hard: he turned the mill, carried wood from the forest, and hauled loads from the fields. The lapdog lived in the house. He knew clever tricks, sat on his master's knee, and whenever the master dined out, he came home with a treat for his dog.

The ass watched all this and grew bitter. Why should that useless little animal be petted while he did all the work? He decided that if he behaved like the lapdog, he would be loved the same way.

One day he broke his halter and galloped into the house. He kicked up his heels and tried to jump around his master just as he had seen the dog do. He smashed the table and the dishes, and then he tried to climb onto his master's lap. The servants, hearing the shouts, rushed in with sticks, beat the ass soundly, and drove him back to the stable, where he lay bruised and sore.
lesson: Every role on a team has its value and its costs. Copying someone else's role out of envy usually means doing it badly and losing respect for the one you had.
people: An ass, a lapdog, their master
source: Aesop's Fables, The Ass and the Lapdog
